# Bug tracker

_Generated from `docs/bugs/bugs.json` with AmiWind v0.0.68-dev8._

The one bug tracker of AmiWind: every bug, its current status, its dated events
and how it was closed. How tracking works, the report template, the closure
steps and the rules: [bug tracking](bugs/README.md). Each bug's full report is
its page in [docs/bugs](bugs/README.md). CHIM engine bugs by part, with the build
each was found in: [CHIM Engine tracker](bugs/CHIM_TRACKER.md).

## Fix index

Generated from [`docs/bugs/bugs.json`](bugs/bugs.json): do not edit this table
by hand. Change the JSON (or use `tools/bug_register.py add` / `set`), then run
`tools/bug_register.py render`. A test fails if the two disagree.

`fixed` means a correction shipped in the named version with supporting
verification; candidates and mitigations stay `open`. `closed` means not a bug,
a duplicate or superseded (the status says which).

| [SESSION-STALL-EMPTY-STATE-READ-67](bugs/SESSION-STALL-EMPTY-STATE-READ-67.md) | A scripted test session ends as a game stall when one read of the game's state comes back empty, although the game runs on | medium | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Fixed in source (903860b4, gate 11760; on the v0.0.67-dev3 line as e14a2590): an empty state reading is read again before any verdict, and an empty realtime with moving ticks is no stall; to be confirmed by sessions that meet a half-written state file. Seen in the every-race light test session of 18 November 2026 (the v0.0.67-dev2 image, the engine of gate 11689): after the Orc woman's take the session ended with "game stalled during () (realtime 745.72 -> )" three seconds after the last command, and the Redguard and Wood Elf takes never ran. The game was running: its state file, read by the same tool, went on from realtime 745.72 and ticks 214463 to 747.87 and 214963 and then 753.43 and 216608, on the game screen, with no error. Cause: the wait check (play) reads the realtime, then the ticks; the realtime read came back empty after its 20 tries (the state file is rewritten in place and stayed half written for those 4 seconds), the ticks read worked and had moved, so the grace wait for a long frame was skipped, and the last line counts an empty realtime as a stall. |

| [ROOM-HALL-OF-MINISTRY-RATS-NOT-DISABLED-67](bugs/ROOM-HALL-OF-MINISTRY-RATS-NOT-DISABLED-67.md) | Mournhold Temple: Hall of Ministry holds seven Infected Rats at the start of a new game, and one attacks: their script should keep them away until the Crimson Plague quest | high | v0.0.67-dev2 (2026_11_18_v0.0.67-dev2_full-mournhold-module-test3_104174c) | open | - | - | - | Open, cause not known (see also EXPANSION-SCRIPTS-NOT-ATTACHED-66). In the per-room check of Mournhold (a new game, the room entered by a debug teleport, the journal empty) the actor list of the Hall of Ministry held seven Infected Rats alive, and one of them attacked on sight. By the game data their script `PlagueHallRat1` disables each of them while the journal `MS_CrimsonPlague` is under 30, enables them at 30 and disables them again from 60. The one rat of the script `PlagueHallRat2` (reference 4219748, disabled while the journal is under 60) was not in the hall, as it should be. So one of the two scripts does its work and the other does not. They differ in two things: `PlagueHallRat1` declares a local variable and has a block for the rat's death that raises the global `PlagueStage`. Both scripts are compiled (neither is in the build's list of scripts left out) and the build's table names the script as bound to all seven rats. To do: the script engine's own lines for these rats (attached or not, the first run, what Disable answered). |

| [MOURNHOLD-BAZAAR-UNDER-WATER-67](bugs/MOURNHOLD-BAZAAR-UNDER-WATER-67.md) | Mournhold's Great Bazaar is under water: the player arrives and walks below a water surface, with the breath bar on, and drowns | critical | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open, fixed in source, not seen in play yet. The streets are above the water (25 to 297); only the canal and the sunken parts lie below it, as in the original. Cause: at the moment a teleport with a height looks for the first surface at or below that height, the street's collision is not loaded yet in this district, and the search ends far below. | [FP-HANDS-PER-RACE-67](bugs/FP-HANDS-PER-RACE-67.md) | In first person the Nord man, the Imperial woman and the Dark Elf and Redguard men show another race's or sex's hand, as the game's records name it, and the skin steps at the wrist | high | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Fixed in source (8308ba5a and f1a962c2 on branch v0.0.67-fpfist, gate 11741); to be confirmed in play on an image built with it. Decided for the project, 2026-11-18: every race and sex draws its own first-person hand, assembled from its own parts through the existing first-person parts pipeline, and no steep colour step at any seam of the arm, whatever the race. A deliberate departure from the original's data, which OpenMW follows: four of the game's first-person hand records name another race's or sex's mesh: b_n_nord_m_hands.1st names b\B_N_Imperial_M_Hands.1st.nif, b_n_imperial_f_hands.1st names b\B_N_Nord_F_Hands.1st.nif, b_n_dark elf_m_hand.1st names b\B_N_Dark Elf_F_Hands.1st.NIF and b_n_redguard_m_hands.1st names b\B_N_Redguard_F_Hands.1st.nif (Morrowind.esm; not changed by Tribunal or Bloodmoon). The game's archive holds each one's own first-person hand mesh (b\b_n_nord_m_hands.1st.nif, b\b_n_imperial_f_hands.1st.nif, b\b_n_dark elf_m_hands.1st.nif, b\b_n_redguard_m_hands.1st.nif: the same 580 triangles, its own skin textures), used by no record; the builder takes that own mesh for these four. The rest of the part table is the race's own records by the original's and OpenMW's order (the sex's first-person part, then its third-person one, then for a woman the man's; the one fallback is the Argonian woman's forearm, the man's). The seam step between the hand and the wrist part, as drawn on the v0.0.67-dev2 image, was up to 55 per channel (the Nord man); with the race's own hand skins it is still up to 40 for some races (the Khajiit woman), and the game's own wrist and forearm parts step by up to 37 (the Khajiit man): the colours are matched along the arm at each seam (the wrist to the forearm, the hand to the wrist), on by default, behind a builder switch whose other setting keeps the original's parts as they are. The measured tables are in FP-BARE-HAND-OTHER-SKIN-67's history. |
| [FP-BARE-HAND-OTHER-SKIN-67](bugs/FP-BARE-HAND-OTHER-SKIN-67.md) | In first person the bare hand of some races has another race's skin and looks gloved, unlike the arm | medium | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Fixed in source (8308ba5a on branch v0.0.67-fpfist, gate 11741 on f1a962c2): the colours are matched along each arm at its seams (the wrist to the forearm, then the hand to the wrist, aiming within 8) and the check measures at the seams (over 16 stops the image), every race and sex; to be confirmed in play on an image built with it. Cause measured: four of the game's first-person hand records (the Nord man's, the Imperial woman's, the Dark Elf and Redguard men's) name another race's or sex's hand mesh and its skin textures, so the drawn hand differs from the arm it meets (the Nord man: 55 per channel at the wrist on v0.0.67-dev2); OpenMW draws those meshes as they are. Commit c1a11300 gives every bare hand its race's and sex's own hand textures (the same as the game's own unused first-person hand meshes) and tints a hand towards its forearm, but its check compared the hand with the forearm while the hand meets the wrist part: at the wrist the step is still up to 40 (the Khajiit woman), and the game's own wrist and forearm parts differ by up to 37 for some races (the Khajiit man). |
| [FP-ARMS-NO-MODEL-SLOT-67](bugs/FP-ARMS-NO-MODEL-SLOT-67.md) | After the race or sex is changed several times in one place, the first-person arms turn into an old hand model with holes and the held lantern is not drawn | medium | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Fixed in source (8308ba5a and f1a962c2 on branch v0.0.67-fpfist, gate 11741): a part model that leaves its set is released at once unless a set still draws it, a refused slot holds off only that outfit, and a race or sex change by any path releases both old sets; to be confirmed in play on an image built with it. Cause read from the session's console (the v0.0.67-dev2 image with the engine of gate 11689, the light test corridor, the race and sex switched in place through Argonian, Breton, Dark Elf, High Elf and Imperial, man and woman each): at the switch to the Khajiit the engine printed "First-person arms from parts: no model slot for progs/parts/cb/619564a20d.mdl (slot 6)" and the same for all eight of the Khajiit's arm parts, then "no part loaded: the baked arms draw", "Hand model slots unavailable; using legacy models" and "First-person held light: no light stance in the arms from parts". From then on, for every later race, the first person drew the legacy hand model (the jagged hand with holes) and no held light (the light rides the arms from parts). Why: the first-person parts are optional models, admitted only while the engine's model table is under its static base or a released slot is free (model.c Mod_CanFindName); every race and sex loads 8 new arm parts and 21 body parts, the parts of the old set are unpinned but never released (aw_view.c hand_parts_ready and parts_ready), and the third-person body loads its parts without that check and grows the table; and one refusal turns the arms from parts off for the whole session (hparts_failed is never reset by a race or outfit change). |
| [DOORS-DISTRICT-FRAMES-NOT-HOLDERS-67](bugs/DOORS-DISTRICT-FRAMES-NOT-HOLDERS-67.md) | The image's door tables knew only the Vvardenfell world's frames: with Mournhold's districts as a world of their own, every door into or out of a district would have stayed closed | high | v0.0.67-dev2 | open | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source. The world door table and the room batches' door links resolve an exterior door or arrival by one holder rule: the town frame whose box holds the point, else the region frame of its cell. The region frames came from the Vvardenfell world's table alone, and the planned cells from the exterior checklist alone. Mournhold's districts are built by the module tribunal-mournhold as a world of their own and installed as a store of their own, so none of their frames was a holder and their cells were not planned: each district door would have been listed as held back. Fix: both tables also take the frames of the worlds the image installs as stores of their own, under the frame map names their install gives them (tools/chim/layer_stores.py frame_holders), and count those cells as planned. To do: read the "Presented districts" line of the first image that holds the districts (doors linked and still held back), and walk a door in each direction in game. |
| [DOOR-CHECK-MODULE-FRAME-MAPS-67](bugs/DOOR-CHECK-MODULE-FRAME-MAPS-67.md) | The image's door check stopped on the first frame map of Mournhold's districts: its table of neighbouring frames knew only the open-world directory | high | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source. The door check walks the player into a door's region frame from a neighbouring frame, and looks both frames up in the open-world directory. Mournhold's districts are a world of their own, with their own frame maps (mh0000 and on) and their own table of rows, so their frames are not in that directory: the check stopped with "KeyError: 'mh0001'" (build_aga.finalize_image, write_door_check, door_engine_check.run, check, job_lines, neighbour_walks). Everything before it had passed: the outdoor world stage, the districts' stage, the towns, the room actors. Fix: a door whose frame is not in the directory the check walks is listed with that reason and not walked; the doors of the island are checked as before. And a first-minute check (module-frame-maps) runs the image's own table code on the frame map names a module will get, before any stage: the engine's map names, the door check's job table and the disk layout. Open: the districts' own doors are not walked by the door check yet (it would need their store in place when it runs); to do with the districts' doors in play. |

| [DISTRICT-PLACED-THINGS-NO-ROW-67](bugs/DISTRICT-PLACED-THINGS-NO-ROW-67.md) | In Mournhold's districts no container, item, activator or door sign can be aimed at: their rows are keyed as a room's, and the game outdoors asks for the cells around the player | high | v0.0.67-dev2 (2026_11_18_v0.0.67-dev2_full-dev3line-test1_a411ea0) | open | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source, not yet seen in the game. Cause: in the game data a district is an interior cell, and the three readers that key placed things by area gave its rows the cell's room number at the original positions. The build presents a district as a block of exterior cells, so the game there is outdoors and asks for the exterior cells around the player: every aim in a courtyard read no rows. By number on the test build's game files: 319 focus rows sat under the five room numbers (Godsreach 73, the Great Bazaar 136, Plaza Brindisi Dorom 47, the Royal Palace courtyard 48, the Temple courtyard 15) and none under the 11 cells of the blocks. Fix: with the build module for the districts, the readers take the districts' cells from one new function (`prepare_focus.cells_presented`), which gives each presented cell as the cells of its block with every placement moved by the one move the presented world itself gets; the focus and item-models stages take the module's receipt and wait for its data stage. The same 319 rows are then under the blocks' keys, the other 2634 keys hold the same rows, and 1212 moved placements equal the presented master's own bytes. A first-minute check holds the counts per district against the districts' own cells, and without the module every reader gives what it gave before (held by tests). To do: on the next test build, open a container, take an item and read an activator in two districts. |

Measured on the v0.0.67-dev2 library, the largest drawing error against the model's size: the cliff racer 3.4 per cent (15.8 of 461 units; fixed on its own whole route in v0.0.67-dev3), three more at 2.8, 2.5 and 1.4 per cent, the other own-table creatures 0.2 to 1.1 per cent. Planned: every creature table holds its own accumulation root (Bip01, else Root Bone, as OpenMW); this re-bakes every creature model and room resident. |

| [BUILD-VISUAL-RECIPES-LAYER-ROWS-KEY-67](bugs/BUILD-VISUAL-RECIPES-LAYER-ROWS-KEY-67.md) | An expansion's visual recipe or cell row re-keyed every base stage that reads the visual recipes: the file was keyed whole | medium | v0.0.67-dev2 | open | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source. A build check listed config/visual-recipes.json among the changed sources of the outdoor world stage, the town stages and the room stages. The changes to that file since the last build were the recipe of Mournhold's districts with its eleven cells and a recipe for four Solstheim cells; no base cell's row and no base recipe had changed. The file was keyed by its bytes. Fix: the visual recipes are a layer-row table like the measured mesh tables: an expansion's cells are named under "layers" and its recipes under "layer_recipes", and a stage that does not read that expansion keys the document without them, so a district recipe, a district cell row or a new district cell moves no base key; the module that builds the districts keys them. One re-key of the stages that read the file follows from the new form itself. Not covered by this entry: the same check also listed changed converter code and the hand-made mesh table among that stage's sources, which are real inputs. To do: compare the outdoor world stage's unit counts and output of the test build with the build before it. |

| [BUILD-MODULE-UNIT-CACHE-IN-KEY-67](bugs/BUILD-MODULE-UNIT-CACHE-IN-KEY-67.md) | The stage of Mournhold's districts was keyed by its own unit cache folder: the units a run stored re-keyed the stage for the next run | medium | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source. The check of a build that resumes a failed one stopped on "the stage would run again ... because its key changed: external_inputs". The stage's only input outside the run folder is its own unit cache folder; the key hashed the folder's files, and the failed run had itself stored its units there (4,076 files), so the run's own key no longer matched. The outdoor world stage's unit cache has been exempt from this since BUILD-CACHE-CHIM-UNITS-33 (every unit there is found by its own key and verified); the new stage's cache was not listed. Fix: the stage's cache is listed as content-addressed, and its row is in the key from the stage's first run on, before the folder exists, so making the folder moves no key either. Open beside it: the other content-addressed caches get their row only once their folder exists; their keys were left as they are. |
| [BUILD-LAYER-SETS-NEVER-TAKEN-67](bugs/BUILD-LAYER-SETS-NEVER-TAKEN-67.md) | A default build with expansions selected took none of their finished outdoor cells: the cell list was resolved before the expansions were selected | high | v0.0.67-dev2 | open | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source. Since v0.0.65 the default cell list was meant to add each selected expansion's named set of cells (Solstheim's for Bloodmoon; Mournhold's districts for Tribunal since the v0.0.67 work), taking the cells the progress tracker calls finished. The list is resolved before the game data check, and the selection was read from the value that check records, so the masters were always empty there and no set was ever added: a test build with all three game files selected listed 1,348 cells in 1,348 frames and 61 dropped, the base list alone, and its plan held no stage for the districts. The unit tests set the recorded value themselves, so they passed. Until then no expansion cell was finished in the tracker, so no earlier build lost anything. Fix: the base world's cell list takes no expansion's set at all (an expansion's cells are built by its own module; Mournhold's districts by the module tribunal-mournhold), the module reads the selection itself, and a first-minute check (expansion-module-cells) names for each selected expansion how many cells the tracker calls finished and which module builds them, and stops the build when finished cells would be left out without a stated reason. To do: confirm in the next test build's first lines (the module's line with 11 district cells, the check's line, the two module stages in the plan). |
| [BUILD-CHECK-READONLY-WORKSPACE-67](bugs/BUILD-CHECK-READONLY-WORKSPACE-67.md) | tools/build.py --check cannot check the reuse plan of a workspace that is mounted read-only: its build preflight stops on the cache folders it cannot write before the reuse plan is made | low | v0.0.67-dev2 | open | - | - | - | Open (18 November 2026). Measured: tools/build.py --check, with and without --reuse-from, against a development workspace and the game data both mounted read-only (and the source tree read-only) stopped after about 90 s in its build preflight, before the reuse plan: tools/build_preflight.py counted every folder of WORKSPACE/cache the build user cannot write (135,451) as a problem, and the room grounding check failed writing the merged master into the checkout (out/scratch, BUILD-MERGED-MASTER-IN-CHECKOUT-66). A check writes no stage index, but it keeps the unit census and the pre-flight analysis in the workspace cache, so it cannot run on a workspace one may only read (a shared or archived one). The stage plan alone runs read only: tools/build.py --reuse-plan RUN and tools/reuse_all.py predict. A fix: a --check reports unwritable cache folders as a note (the build keeps its stop) and writes no cache bookkeeping, and the merged master leaves the checkout (BUILD-MERGED-MASTER-IN-CHECKOUT-66). |
| [BUILD-ACTOR-LIBRARY-SHARE-RACE-67](bugs/BUILD-ACTOR-LIBRARY-SHARE-RACE-67.md) | The actor library stage's two pools wrote their worker share through one temporary file name: a write found its file gone | low | v0.0.67-dev2 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source. While the creatures bake beside the NPCs, the stage keeps a share file for the NPC pool (the stage's allowance less the creature workers) and rewrites it every half second; when the creatures end, their callback writes it once more from another thread. Both wrote through one temporary file and replaced the share file with it, so the second replace could find the temporary file gone: a build log showed "exception calling callback" with a file-not-found error on that temporary name. The name was the share file's with its suffix replaced, which is also the name the scheduler writes the stage's own allowance through. Fix: one writer at a time (a lock), and a temporary name of the share file's own, with the process number. |

| [MESH-TABLE-SECOND-LAYER-REKEY-67](bugs/MESH-TABLE-SECOND-LAYER-REKEY-67.md) | A row of a second expansion in a measured mesh table would re-key every unit recorded with the first expansion's rows | high | v0.0.67-dev1 | open | - | - | - | Fixed in source, to be confirmed by the unit check of the first build with a Tribunal row. A layer's list is now append-only (new rows at its end), and a whole-table record also matches the table with any first part of each layer's list; a layer row changed, removed or put anywhere but the end still misses, and so does a mesh's own row for the units that looked it up (tests/test_mesh_table_layer_rows.py). |

| [CHIMPORT-CELL-KEY-REQUEST-ID-67](bugs/CHIMPORT-CELL-KEY-REQUEST-ID-67.md) | The CHIM import keys every cell by the master builder request that runs it | medium | v0.0.67-dev1 | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Found by reading the code on 17 November 2026: the CHIM import's cell key (tools/chimport.py cell_key, the key a whole cell is linked by from the shared storage pool) takes in every AMIWIND_ setting of its process except a short list (CELL_KEY_IGNORED_ENV), and that list leaves out AMIWIND_AW_REQUEST, which the master builder's CHIM import route sets to each request's own id (tools/aw_service.py). The build's own stage keys leave that setting out as bookkeeping (tools/build_cache.py IGNORED_ENV). | [UI-NO-SHARED-LAYOUT-67](bugs/UI-NO-SHARED-LAYOUT-67.md) | Menus place their boxes and buttons at fixed pixel positions of their own, so margins differ from screen to screen and buttons sit against the bottom edge of the box | medium | v0.0.66 (2026_11_17_v0.0.66_full-v0.0.66-release-try2_ad5e9a0) | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open. | [TP-BEING-TRIBUNAL-FALLS-THROUGH-67](bugs/TP-BEING-TRIBUNAL-FALLS-THROUGH-67.md) | Teleporting to a character in some Tribunal interiors drops the player through the floor (the pawnbroker Ten-Tongues Weerhat, the Assassin) | high | v0.0.66 (v0.0.67-dev1) | open | - | - | - | Open; fixed in source on the v0.0.67-opening branch, to be confirmed in play. Cause (found 2026-11-17 by number): a Beings row of the teleport list holds the character's placed point, its feet on the floor, in the room's units. The teleport handed that point to the room load as the arrival, which is the player's origin, 16.875 units over the floor for every door into a room. The arrival search looks for a floor from 8 units over the arrival down to 88 under it, so its first standing box stood inside the floor and it took the next floor under the room, or found none. Measured on the v0.0.67-dev1 image with tools/tp_arrivals.py (all 6,182 room arrivals of the image, the room collision as the image checks read it): from the feet, 1,302 of 3,623 being arrivals land under their floor (base game 1,166 of 3,092, Tribunal 103 of 281, Bloodmoon 33 of 250; Ten-Tongues Weerhat 64 units under the pawnbroker's floor, the Assassin row's room placements 69 under) and 1,553 find no floor. Every teleport to a room (its own start, 1,329) and every door arrival into a room (1,240) lands on its floor in every layer, which is why a teleport to a Tribunal Dwemer ruin works. When the character is in the room at arrival, the teleport then moves the player to a free spot beside it, which can hide the fault; why it showed in Tribunal first is to be confirmed in play. Fix: the engine lifts a being's point to a door arrival's height before the room load (aw_listbox_rules.c AW_TpBeingArrival); with it, 0 of the 6,182 arrivals land under a floor (140 being arrivals still find no standing spot at the point, a cage or a tight corner; they fall back to the room's start and then to the spot beside the character). Guard: tools/tp_arrivals.py on an image (exit 1 on any arrival under its floor) and tests/test_tp_arrivals.py in every gate. The arrival step itself was checked: the room's collision is primed at the arrival before the search runs (the CHIM spawn), and the search does put the player on the floor it finds; the fault was the height it was handed. Outdoors a being's point stays its feet, as the coordinate teleport expects. |

The container count reads a frame's own exports as drawn. It changes the CHIM world's Seyda Neen frame, so it comes with a build of its own; to be counted on that build and seen in game. The v0.0.67-dev2 build's Seyda Neen town stage refused these containers (its statics comparison did not count the frame's declared additions of this kind): fixed in source on branch v0.0.67-seydatown, with an early check of the frame against the town after the bsp stage. |

Seen in a played game of the v0.0.66 release: no autosave was written. A scripted run of v0.0.67-dev1 still writes one on every map change, so the cause is on the player's path, not in the save itself. | [REUSE-STOP-OLD-GROUPS-67](bugs/REUSE-STOP-OLD-GROUPS-67.md) | The strict reuse check counts the units an older version of a bake left in its cache as work the build would redo, so a one-unit table with history stops a build that would reuse it | medium | v0.0.66 (2026_11_17_v0.0.66_full-v0.0.66-release_ad5e9a0) | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open; fixed in source in v0.0.67-dev1 (586fd07f, gate 11073); to be confirmed by the first --reuse-all-available build that holds it. The check stopped the engine and image stages with "would bake again 6 of the 7 units its unit cache npc-voice-table holds" while the build needs one table, stored under its unchanged key. Cause: the stop counted the units a cache holds as its largest group under one key; the voice table is looked up once per build and keeps one unit for each set of game files its key saw, each stored by another build. Fix: every stored unit names the build that stored it, and the units one build looks up are the largest group bounded by the most units one build stored under one key (a table: 1; the first-person parts: 579). Measured on the real caches with the release's keys: npc-voice-table 1 of 7 (a stop) becomes 1 of 1; the other caches keep their counts. |
| [PRISON-SHIP-TABLE-DARK-TRIANGLE-67](bugs/PRISON-SHIP-TABLE-DARK-TRIANGLE-67.md) | A large dark triangle lies across the table in the prison ship hold | medium | v0.0.66 (2026_11_17_v0.0.66_full-v0.0.66-release-try2_ad5e9a0) | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open; cause found 2026-11-18 by number, fixed in source on the v0.0.67-dev3 line (fac3d8f7), not yet checked in play. The triangle is not a shadow or a decal: it is one of the table's two iron bands (a thin sleeve of 40 faces around the table top). The hold's visual reduction, which keeps the shell's structural shapes and reduces the rest to 8 per cent, left each band 4 faces: two slanted two-sided planes rising 1.6 units over the band and past its side, dark iron across the table top. The four tables of the hold had it. The fix keeps the bands whole through the reduction and draws each as its box, six faces spanning it exactly (tools/room_map_shapes.py, --room-shapes, on by default): 8 to 12 faces a table. |

The tile is the foot of the ship's mast: the hold's visual reduction kept the shell's structural shapes whole and reduced the rest to 8 per cent, and the mast (a five-sided column of 30 faces, on the upper deck and again on the lower deck) went to 4 faces while its authored collision column stayed, so the player walked into an invisible post with only the tile at its foot drawn. A check of every collision piece against the drawn faces at its place (tools/drawn_collision.py) found 62 such pieces on the v0.0.67-dev2 hold, 40 of them taller than a step: the two masts, the raised deck at both ends of the hold, a lower-deck post, a pole by the stairs and four side boards of the stairs. The fix draws those shapes whole, by their exact names, in the room map's own preparation (tools/room_map_shapes.py, --room-shapes, on by default): the shell 7,997 to 8,308 drawn faces (+3.9 per cent), the collision unchanged, the check 62 lost (40 standing) to 1 lost (0 standing; the end of a support beam 7 units tall, under a step). The interior stage now stops on any collision piece taller than a step that the original draws and the room does not. |

| [HUD-TEXTS-OVERLAP-67](bugs/HUD-TEXTS-OVERLAP-67.md) | Two texts are drawn on top of each other in the HUD: the name of the aimed character and the place name | medium | v0.0.66 (2026_11_17_v0.0.66_full-v0.0.66-release-try2_ad5e9a0) | open (fixed in source) | - | - | - | Open. Seen on the v0.0.66 release: aiming at the clerk of the Census and Excise Office draws his name over the text Seyda Neen at the top right, with the key hint Enter: E under it; the location title of the HUD reads Census and Excise Office, so the second text is not the location title but the label of the door behind the clerk (the exit to Seyda Neen). Cause, read in the engine (engine/aga/src/aw_scene.c AW_SceneDraw): two pickers feed two labels that do not know of each other. The person's name comes from AW_SceneTargetName through npc_target, which takes the nearest person along the view ray (the ray against his model box within reach, FOCUS-NPC-OVERRIDES-ITEM-62), not a radius around the player; it is drawn first, whatever else is aimed. The door label and its action come from aimed_door, whose wall trace ignores people (MOVE_NOMONSTERS), so a door behind a person is aimed through him and its label and action draw in the same corner. Engine-wide, the label of a person therefore competes with the label of whatever else the crosshair meets. Planned rule: one label at a time, the aimed one first: the nearest thing along the view ray among person, door, item and plant decides, and only its label shows; a door behind a person is not aimed. Also a test that fails when two HUD texts share screen space, with a priority order of who yields, built on the shared layout of UI-NO-SHARED-LAYOUT-67. |

| [EMU-WARP-STARVES-GAME-CPU-67](bugs/EMU-WARP-STARVES-GAME-CPU-67.md) | In the emulator's warp mode the game gets far less processor time per second of its own clock, so its frames take seconds of game time | low | v0.0.66 (2026_11_17_v0.0.66_full-v0.0.66-release-try2_ad5e9a0) | open | - | - | - | Open, low (the test method, not the game). Measured on the v0.0.66 release image with the opening journey, FS-UAE 3.1.66, JIT 68040 preset, 32 MB Fast. Without warp the engine clock follows the real one (956.5 s in 956.6 s) and the journey passed 42/42. With warp_mode = 1 the engine clock ran 467.6 s in the first 15 host s, the menu frames took 5.6 to 6.6 s of it each and the first map load stopped on the test console folder stall. With uae_warp_limit = 100 (twice a PAL machine's pace) and the deterministic option the menu ran at 1.8 times the real pace, but the start took 46 s (17 s without warp) and the first load's frame 151.0 s of engine clock (5.6 s without warp, the same 470 file calls), about 75 host s against about 6. Cause in the emulator: in warp the processor at its fastest setting runs only within the frame's time base (custom.cpp 1399-1407) and every emulated frame costs host time of its own. Warp is not used to speed up the test sessions; numbers in docs/performance/EMULATOR-WARP.md. |

| [MWSCRIPT-SETHEALTH-ZERO-NO-DEATH-66](bugs/MWSCRIPT-SETHEALTH-ZERO-NO-DEATH-66.md) | A script's SetHealth 0 leaves the actor alive: its health reads 0 but it stays standing and fighting (Dagoth Ur after the end script, the dreamer workers after the Heart) | high | v0.0.66-dev10 (2026_11_16_v0.0.66-dev10_full-v0.0.66-dev10_f446092) | open | - | - | - | Found 16 November 2026 (the endgame session ENDGAME-HEART-SESSION-66, run2 on the v0.0.66-dev10 image): after the end script's "Dagoth_Ur_2"->SetHealth 0, dagoth_ur_2->gethealth read 0 while the actor list showed him fighting and the console said he cannot reach the player and flees; the three dreamer workers, whose script sets their health to 0 once HeartDestroyed is 1, stayed alive in the list (the end script later hid them). SetHealth sets the base and the current to 0 (AW_ActorSetStat, as OpenMW OpSetDynamic), and host_actor kills only while the base is above 0 (dyn_cur <= 0 and dyn_base > 0). OpenMW 0.51 CreatureStats::setDynamic: a current health under 1 is death, whatever the base. Fixed in source on 16 November 2026 (commit 7024bf28 on the v0.0.66 line, not gated yet), covered by tests, to be confirmed by the end-of-quest session on the dev11 image. One rule for every path, as OpenMW 0.51 (creaturestats.cpp setDynamic, statsextensions.cpp OpSetDynamic): a current health under 1 is death, whatever the base (aw_actorstate.h AW_ACTOR_HEALTH_DEAD). A script's SetHealth, ModHealth or ModCurrentHealth that takes a living NPC or creature under 1 kills it once, as a blow would: the record's death (AW_ActorHealthDeath: OnDeath, the dead count, an essential character's box) and, when its place is loaded, the fight's death or the body a fight leaves (host_actor, as a fall's death does). The same rule now decides a blow's death (aw_combat_rules.c AW_CombatSwing), a spell's and its ticks' (aw_mwhost.c, aw_combat.c AW_CombatSpellHit) and a fall's (aw_fall.c): each killed only at 0 or below before, so an actor left at 0.5 lived. A record already under 1 before the change (a body the data places with no health) is not killed again. Not changed: the player's own death outside a blow (world damage, a script, a spell: at 0 or below, the engine's rule). Tests: tests/test_actor_death_native.py with tests/aga_actor_death_test.c (the real actor record and blow rule): SetHealth 0 on a living actor kills it once; actors taken to 0.5 by SetHealth, ModHealth and ModCurrentHealth die; actors left at 1 live; a dead actor's SetHealth 0 and a body with no health die no second time; a blow that leaves 0.5 kills and one that leaves 1 does not; and the wiring of each path. Reach. Counted in the v0.0.66-dev10 script file (mwscript.awm, SHA-256 e7502ad4336cd1d2): 98 health calls in 57 scripts; 41 set a constant health under 1 in 28 scripts, 39 of them on an NPC or a creature in 26 scripts: EndGame (Dagoth Ur and the seven ash vampires), dreamerWorkerScript, ashvampire, drowned, the six skaalwere scripts, SadriThief, trackerScript, the fabricant and centurion fight (cent_fab_attack, fab_cent_attack, fab_cent_fight_die), ColonyFalco, ErichScript, JeleenScript, ThirskCorpse, ThirskSvenjaDeath, Warlord_aScript, boneScript, drownOnExit and three dialogue results. |

| [WANDER-DOOR-RULE-66](bugs/WANDER-DOOR-RULE-66.md) | A wandering resident can stop at a destination right by a door and stand there; the original sends an idle wanderer near a door walking | medium | v0.0.66-dev7 (2026_11_15_v0.0.66-dev7_full-v0.0.66-dev7_a33bba9) | open (confirmed by a test) | - | - | deferred | REGRESSED in v0.0.66-dev12 (fixed in v0.0.66-dev11 before): The v0.0.66-dev12 opening journey (ac37e80b) stopped part B in step 9 as the dev10 journey had: the use key aimed at the door 113833 went to the actor Fargoth standing in front of it (focus row 164) in 13 tries around pitch 9.9 and yaw 264.5; the dev11 journey had passed once. One passing run does not confirm a fix that depends on where actors walk.. Before: Closed: fixed in source (237b5a6f, gate 10941), shipped in v0.0.66-dev11, confirmed in play by the opening journey's step 9 on that build. Confirmed in play on v0.0.66-dev11 (26ed570f, gate 10941): the opening journey passed 42 of 42 checks, and its step 9 went through the Census and Excise Office's street door (113833) in Seyda Neen with no resident in the way (on dev10 the aim at that door went to Fargoth, `fargoth`, in 12 of 13 tries). Fixed in v0.0.66-dev11. Before: Fixed in source, covered by tests, to be confirmed by the next opening journey. Cause: the residents' Wander packages (engine/aga/src/aw_ambient.c) had no door rule, so a wanderer whose destination lay right by a door stood there through its idles, in front of the door and on its arrival point. The original sends such a wanderer on: OpenMW 0.51 checks an idle wanderer every 1.5 seconds and sends it walking when it faces a door within 1.6 times the activation distance (aiwander.cpp onIdleStatePerFrameActions; obstacle.cpp proximityToDoor: at most 60 degrees off its facing, heights left out, only a door that is shut and still), and a walker that has to evade with a door within the activation distance drops that destination and the allowed ones on its path and takes another (aiwander.cpp evadeObstacles, trimAllowedPositions). Seen: in the v0.0.66-dev6 and dev7 opening journeys the guard (reference 128967) stood by the street door of the Census and Excise Office (113833) in Seyda Neen; in the v0.0.66-dev10 journey Fargoth (fargoth, 128964) stood 55 units from that door's reference and 12 of the 13 aims at the door in step 9 went to him. The fix, for every wanderer and every door: both checks in aw_ambient.c, against the place's load doors at their references' positions (the focus table's door rows, aw_inventory.c AW_PlacedDoors) and the map's hinged doors that stand shut and still (aw_hinged_door.c AW_HingedDoorShut); a disabled door never counts; a resident with wander distance 0, or one that only walks to spots near its start, stays as before. "chim actors ambient doors on" is the default in id1/default-game.cfg; "chim actors ambient doors off" gives the old behaviour back; "chim actors ambient" prints the checks. Tests: tests/aga_ambient_test.c (a door ahead within the distance and 60 degrees; facing away or farther stays idle; no check without a distance or routes; a stuck walker drops its destination and those on its route and never picks them again) and tests/test_ambient_lut.py. The next opening journey should show step 9 aimed at the street door with no resident named by the aim, and the doors line of "chim actors ambient" with idle residents sent on. |

| [DOOR-ARRIVAL-INSIDE-ACTOR-66](bugs/DOOR-ARRIVAL-INSIDE-ACTOR-66.md) | Coming back out of the census office onto the Seyda Neen street after a kill, the player arrives inside the guard who has walked to the door and stays stuck | medium | v0.0.66-dev5 (2026_11_15_v0.0.66-dev5_full-v0.0.66-dev5_18eb63f) | open | - | - | - | Fixed in source, covered by tests, to be confirmed in play (branch v0.0.66-doorarrival). Cause: outdoors the scene's actors join after the arrival's check: they are queued with the arrival's ring, spawned over the next ticks and then moved to where the saved changes left them. The guard (reference 128967), who walks by his Wander package, had walked to the street door while the player was inside (WANDER-DOOR-RULE-66; in the dev6 journey he already stood in front of that door before step 6; no crime was involved: the journey's console kill is not counted as the player's crime and nobody pursued), and came back 8 units from the arrival point, his box overlapping the player's by 6.2 units across. Quake's box clip then held both: a sweep that starts inside the sum of two boxes is solid until one frame's move leaves it whole and the walk zeroes the velocity, and the stuck search, which counted every body, failed in every frame ("player is stuck.", up to 164 position tests each time). A player could not walk out: in the native test at the measured boxes and positions, ten frames of walking away moved the player 0 units. The fix, for every door, teleport and actor: two bodies that already overlap collide as the original game's actors do (OpenMW 0.51 actorconvexcallback.cpp): only a move toward the other's centre stops, so they walk apart (engine/aga/src/world.c AW_BodyOverlap, aw_body_overlap 1); the stuck search leaves other bodies out (SV_TestWorldPosition); and for three seconds after an arrival an actor that joins onto the player steps the player once to the nearest clear standing spot beside the point (aw_scene.c, aw_arrival_clear 1, the console line "Arrival: ... stood on the arrival point"). Both are on in id1/default-game.cfg; 0 gives the old behaviour back. Tests: tests/aga_body_overlap_test.c (walking away: 30 units in ten frames, no stuck search) and the arrival case in tests/aga_scene_test.c. The next opening journey should print that Arrival line after step 6's return (or none, if the guard stands elsewhere) and no "player is stuck." lines. The v0.0.66-dev9 journey did not exercise the case: with the victim fixed in the west of the town, no actor stood on the street door's arrival point after step 6 (no "Arrival:" line) and the console of neither part has a "player is stuck." line, so the fix has not been seen at work and the entry stays open. |

| [SAVE-SCRIPT-ROW-HINT-ONLY-65](bugs/SAVE-SCRIPT-ROW-HINT-ONLY-65.md) | A saved script's values are matched to the compiled script only by its row: a rebuild in another order drops them | high | v0.0.65 | open (shipped, awaiting confirmation) | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source (a3d8708f, gate 10211) and shipped in v0.0.66-dev2; awaiting confirmation: a save made on one numbered build loaded on a later one whose scripts were rebuilt in another order, with its script values back by name. Before: The fix: a saved script is found by its name (the saved row only tried first; a rebuilt file finds a moved script with one read of every row's name hash), and every saved script value now carries its variable's name and type, with a signature of the script's variables. While a script's variables are as saved, values go back by their slot; when a rebuild inserted, removed, reordered or retyped them, each value goes to the variable of its name (converted between whole numbers and floats as the original engine does); a value whose variable is gone is left out and counted, and the load says so in one line. Two names that share a hash are never mixed: the builder refuses such script, global and quest names, and two variables of one script that share one are restored only while the script is unchanged. Older saves load by slot as before. |
| [SAVE-EXPORT-FAILURE-ACCEPTED-65](bugs/SAVE-EXPORT-FAILURE-ACCEPTED-65.md) | A save is written as good although the changed actors or script values failed to go into it | high | v0.0.65 | open (shipped, awaiting confirmation) | - | - | - | Open: fixed in source (4b32d948, gate 10210; its follow-ups in v0.0.66-dev3) and shipped in v0.0.66-dev2; awaiting confirmation: in play on a numbered build, a save whose part cannot be kept is refused with the line naming the part and the previous save unchanged (the opening journey's quicksave shows saves still work, not a refusal). Before: The fix: every part of a save reports whether it was kept, and any failure refuses that save with one line naming the part: the changed actor records, the script values, the globals, the quest stages, the known topics (also when their name table cannot be read), the references' identities, the actors' and the objects' changes, the actor block, the dated journal and the generation number. A row the world change list refuses while the save is taken refuses it too, whatever the part reported. Nothing of a refused save is written: the previous save stays as it was and the game goes on unchanged. A native test runs the real save path with each part forced to fail in turn (and with refused rows) and checks that the previous save file is unchanged byte for byte, no other is written and the line names the part. |

Cause before: the combat AI had no spell action at all; the actor table already held every actor's spell list. Not rated yet: Burden, Feather, Dispel, the cures, Restore Magicka, the bound longbow; fights between two characters use weapons only. Tracker NPC-NO-SPELLCASTING-65; Dagoth Ur's missing run and attack animations stay DAGOTH-UR-NO-ANIMATIONS-65. Added 16 November 2026: the payment of the magicka described above was missing until NPC-CAST-MAGICKA-NOT-PAID-66 was repaired on the v0.0.66 line (the call named the wrong stat, so a caster that could afford a spell once cast it every time). |

| [CHIM-SOL-FLORA-PATH-64](bugs/CHIM-SOL-FLORA-PATH-64.md) | The Solstheim test frame converts its trees as full models, not through the world flora cards Vvardenfell uses | high | v0.0.64 (v0.0.64 Solstheim test frame (chim-sol)) | open | - | - | - | Open: the expansions have no path through the island's build pipeline. The --dlc and --no-dlc options only record the chosen layers; the one expansion path is the test-only Solstheim stage, which runs the CHIM world step alone on chosen cells: none of the world terrain, scenery, flora card, harvest, room, resident or NPC stages, and none of their reductions. So every Bloodmoon tree went in as its full model (472 to 724 faces) and the views drew 45,964 faces at the median against 7,562 on Vvardenfell: not a like-for-like comparison. Fix: each layer is built by the same stages as Vvardenfell, exteriors and interiors, with every optimization, keyed by the layer's own files; then measured again. |

| [BUILD-UNIT-KEYS-REACH-64](bugs/BUILD-UNIT-KEYS-REACH-64.md) | New collision settings re-keyed the NPC, creature, player-body and resident unit caches, which never read them | high | v0.0.64-dev5 | open | - | - | deferred | Fixed on the v0.0.64-unitkeys branch. Two causes. (1) The hollow bevels and collision mesh settings were added to mesh_geometry_env.py and collision_source_env.py as top-level constants; import-time code counts in the key of every function of a module, so every bake importing them was re-keyed. They now live in hollow_bevels_env.py and collision_mesh_env.py, and the two modules are byte-identical to v0.0.64-dev4 again. (2) A unit key counted every setting name its reach holds as text, including names held only in a constant no reached code uses, so the model hull default change (chain to auto) would have re-keyed every NPC and creature bake. A setting now counts only where the reached code names it; units stored under the older form are looked up under it and stored again. The residents still read the model hull by their reach (the resident pool key reads mesh_geometry_env whole) and are re-baked. Seen again in v0.0.66-dev1: with the merging reader of the base game and both expansions, every unit cache of the build would bake again in full (2,147 of 2,147 resident bakes, 2,064 of 2,064 scenery regions, 1,931 of 1,931 flora regions, 2,158 of 2,158 player parts, 1,059 of 1,059 room batches and more), also for the cells, rooms and actors the expansions do not change: a unit key takes its stage's whole game input and source closure, not the records the unit reads. The build stopped at its reuse guard after 12 minutes and was run again with the full bake allowed for 13 stages. Seen again on the v0.0.66-dev1 build (13 November 2026): the new merging reader of the expansions is in every unit key, so with the expansions switched off (the same data as v0.0.65) all 1,769 room batches bake again, about 14 to 16 seconds each, about 7 hours, besides 12 more stages. Wanted: a unit keyed by what the reader gives it for the masters loaded (the decoded records), not by the reader's code. |
| [BUILD-PREFLIGHT-SETTING-VALUES-64](bugs/BUILD-PREFLIGHT-SETTING-VALUES-64.md) | The reuse check counted unit caches by their code digest only: a changed setting value could still bake every unit again after a clean check | high | v0.0.64-dev5 | open | - | - | - | Open. A unit key is the code digest plus the options, and the options hold the values of the AMIWIND_* settings in reach (the model hull mode, for instance). The check groups stored units by the code digest alone, so a change of a setting value is not seen before the stage runs. To do: count stored units by their recorded options digest too, with the settings the build exports. |

| [ROOM-LOAD-KEEPS-EXTERIOR-CACHE-64](bugs/ROOM-LOAD-KEEPS-EXTERIOR-CACHE-64.md) | Entering a large room from a town keeps the town's CHIM model cache, so the room can run out of Fast RAM at 32 MB although it fits on its own | high | v0.0.64-dev2 (MiniWind v0.0.64-dev2 akulakhan-chamber try3) | open | - | - | - | Corrected 10 November 2026 after reading the room grow (chim_world.c Chim_RoomGrow, chim_room.c RoomPreGrow): the 3,888,880 bytes of "cache" in the heap line are the Quake cache inside the Hunk gap, which the room's Hunk allocations evict; and the town's 6 MiB CHIM model bank is already counted in what the zone and banks give (12,775 KiB at the first try). What is short is Fast RAM outside the Hunk: 12 MiB were free at boot, 6 MiB went to the CHIM bank, and after Balmora only 3,011 KiB are free when the room asks (74 KiB given back by the re-makeable releasers; 492 KiB on the second try). So about 3 MB of Fast RAM stays with something Balmora loaded. The room's Hunk step takes 2,012 KiB (the zone, chim_reserve_kib 2,048 KiB and 1,553 KiB for the map's rest take the remainder); with the 3 MB the room would fit. Next: a per-owner count of the Fast RAM in use before and after the map change (aw_memcensus), then give the holder back at a room load or make it re-makeable. |

| [CHIM-STORE-ONE-AT-A-TIME-64](bugs/CHIM-STORE-ONE-AT-A-TIME-64.md) | The engine streams one CHIM store at a time, so frames of a second store cannot sit beside the first in the open world | high | v0.0.64-dev2 (2026_11_10_v0.0.64-dev2_miniwind-solstheim) | open | - | - | - | Open. Solstheim belongs to the same exterior world as Vvardenfell, on the same cell grid, north-west of it, with open sea between. Today a CHIM map names its store and Chim_StoreSelect refuses to change store while a CHIM map runs; model, texture and file ids belong to one store. A Solstheim frame kept in its own store (chimsol, the test image) therefore loads only as a separate map, not streamed next to the Vvardenfell frames. Way out without re-keying the base world: one exterior index whose base part is byte-identical and whose Solstheim frames, models and textures are appended after the base ids (an image-side merge of the two indexes), or an engine that keeps both indexes and looks a frame up by its cell in either. |

| [UNDERWATER-BREATH-62](bugs/UNDERWATER-BREATH-62.md) | Underwater there is no breath meter and no drowning, and Water Breathing is not applied | high | v0.0.62-dev1 | open | - | - | - | v0.0.63 release check, round two: an Argonian read Water Breathing 0 at the start, after a load and after a teleport, and drowned in the Seyda Neen bay. Cause found: in the original game data the Argonian race spell "argonian breathing" is a castable spell (Water Breathing for 120 s on self, always succeeds), not a constant ability; OpenMW gives the race's spells to the player's spell list the same way, and a castable spell works only when it is cast. Water Breathing 0 before casting it is therefore the original behaviour; the check expected a constant effect. The engine keeps the spell in the list (character creation, a race change, a loaded game: fix fb279aeb). The in-game check is now: the player knows the spell, casts it, reads Water Breathing 1 for 120 s and does not drown. Cause found in v0.0.64 (round three): the console's sorted id lookup treated a successful read of the actor table as a failure, so player->getspell answered 0 for every spell, also for a player holding the race power; fixed in the engine (the read is checked the right way round), with a test of every call site. |

| [SESSION-STALL-AFTER-LONG-FRAME-62](bugs/SESSION-STALL-AFTER-LONG-FRAME-62.md) | The game stops with its clock frozen right after a frame of several seconds spent on console output or file reads, in three of ten scripted Seyda Neen sessions | high | v0.0.62-dev1 (MiniWind v0.0.62-dev1 seyda-enabledraw2 7bb679e) | open | - | - | deferred | REGRESSED in v0.0.64-dev3 (fixed in v0.0.62-dev1 before): Seen again once in a scripted Akulakhan Chamber MiniWind session (commit 86c595a5, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB Fast): after the room load failed and the console teleport back to Balmora, a 1,448 ms frame, then the game stopped at the console picture with the program counter in the idle loop (pc 401D7FC4, 1 of 5 samples) and no file call in progress.. Before: Fixed in v0.0.62-dev1 (7 November 2026). The game did not hang: each stop was a long frame that the session judged too early. With the remote console on, every console print was its own open, seek, write and close on the emulator's remote-console folder, and one "edict" listing is about 300 prints (each field name is padded one space at a time): 1 to 1.2 seconds a listing on a quiet machine, 3 to 7 seconds on a loaded one. The processor samples were idle because the game was waiting on those folder writes. The session wait then called a stall after 1 second whenever neither the game clock nor the engine's ticks moved, although the state file is written only between frames and on the heartbeat; the third session was a 6.8-second frame of script file reads after "dbg mwscript result". Repair: console prints collect in memory and reach the log in one append twice a second (and on the heartbeat, when the 8 KiB buffer is full and at exit), so an edict listing no longer makes a long frame (REMOTE-CONSOLE-LOG-COST-32); the session wait gives a frame without a heartbeat 30 seconds (STALL_GRACE) before the stall examination and logs it as a long frame. Verified: 10 of 10 scripted Seyda Neen sessions (32 MB Fast, JIT) with the same edict prints and "dbg mwscript result" ran without a stop; every script-file frame of 4.6 to 8.4 seconds was logged as a long frame and the session went on. That frame itself is still long and is not part of this repair. |

Seen three times in v0.0.62-dev1 (the candle beside Sellus Gravius in the Census and Excise Office, the bracket fungi on the Bitter Coast trees with a character near, Tarhiel's journal beside his body) and again in v0.0.67-dev1 and v0.0.67-dev2 (a person won over a door behind him; Fargoth and a guard took the use key at the census office's street door; Aleri Aren at the door back to the courtyard in the Mournhold Guards' Quarters). Causes: until v0.0.62 the actor test came first, so any actor whose box the view ray met took the key wherever the item lay; until v0.0.67-dev2 the load door and the person were chosen by two separate tests; and a person's model has stored one frame since v0.0.52 whose box encloses every pose, about 60 units long around a body about 15 wide, so his box reached a door or an item beside him. Expected, as in the reference engine: activation takes the nearest object along the view ray within the activation distance, tested against the drawn body, never the nearest character. Fixed in source: one focus a frame, the nearest thing along the view ray (f6147af6, gate 11384), and a person's use box from his body (branch v0.0.67-focusbox): the collision hull's half widths 7.32 by 7.12 times his scale, never wider than the stored box, the stored height kept; a body by the stored box lowered to 8 units over its floor; creatures and models with more frames keep their box. Host tests by number (tests/aga_activate_rules_test.c, tests/aga_npc_contact_test.c), and aw_placed aim prints the choice. Waiting for the in-game check. Related: FOCUS-REACH-ITEM-ORIGIN-58, FOCUS-BOX-UNDRAWN-ITEMS-58, CENSUS-INTRO-SCRIPTS-62, HARVEST-SEYDA-TREE-SPRITE-BLOCKS-PICK-47, CORPSE-INVENTORY-NOT-OPENABLE-59, HUD-TEXTS-OVERLAP-67. The converter marks every texture whose alpha channel leaves at least 1 % of its texels under half alpha (name prefix "{", palette index 255 for its transparent texels; other textures keep their bytes and unit keys), and the engine draws those faces in a separate pass after the walls, z-tested, skipping index 255 (aw_fence, dbg fence; off by default until a measured A/B on the next full build decides). Proof pending: the cobweb in Andrano Ancestral Tomb and a hanging growth outdoors with the switch off and on. Earlier: Open, PERSISTING (reported on the v0.0.61 release image and again in v0.0.62-dev1). The whole alpha path for planes and decals is suspect, indoors and outdoors alike: every alpha-tested texture in rooms and in the open world is to be checked, not only the cobweb, and fixed for every see-through surface of the game. Wider title for the work: alpha-tested planes and decals draw opaque, indoors and outdoors (tracker ROOM-DECAL-ALPHA-62). |

| [BUILD-VERSION-HEADER-RACE-61](bugs/BUILD-VERSION-HEADER-RACE-61.md) | An engine build can stop on the warning that the generated CHIM version header is shorter than expected | medium | v0.0.61-dev2 | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker GAME-RECORDER-61, a side finding). Cause: the heap header's make rule runs the version generator on every make (its heap-size-check prerequisite is always out of date), beside the compiles, and the generator rewrote amiwind_version.h, chim_version.h and amiwind_version.i every time, so a compile could read one half written. | [SAVE-EFFECTS-BLOCK-SIZE-61](bugs/SAVE-EFFECTS-BLOCK-SIZE-61.md) | Loading a save with a spell effect active loses the effects and the made spells, enchanted items, soul gems and other blocks saved after them | high | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61, fixed on the v0.0.61-magicitems line, waiting for a numbered build. | [PLAYER-FORTIFY-END-AS-DAMAGE-61](bugs/PLAYER-FORTIFY-END-AS-DAMAGE-61.md) | When a Fortify Attribute effect on the player ends, the character sheet keeps it as a raised modifier and records the drop as damage | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61. The sheet keeps one modifier per attribute (the race and birthsign fortify) and a damage value. A Fortify Attribute on the player raises the modifier; when it ends, the lower value is stored as damage instead of lowering the modifier again. The shown attribute is right, but the damage can be restored by a Restore Attribute effect, which leaves the attribute raised for good. Worn Constant Effect items that fortify an attribute make it happen at every change of gear. Planned: the effects' share of the modifier kept apart from the sheet's own. |

| [GODMODE-COMBAT-DAMAGE-61](bugs/GODMODE-COMBAT-DAMAGE-61.md) | With god mode on, a fight's blows still take the player's health and kill the player | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Checked in part on the v0.0.61-dev2 image on 6 November 2026 at 32 MB Fast: with god mode on, the Samarys ancestor ghost's blows that hit took 0.0 health (three hits), and with it off the same blows took 1.0 to 3.7 health each. Not yet checked: god mode kept across a map load (fact 2 below). Before: Open, v0.0.61; corrected 6 November 2026. Two facts: (1) the combat layer takes a blow's damage on its own fighter sheet and never reads Quake's god flag (aw_combat.c has no FL_GODMODE check), so god mode cannot stop a fight's blows; (2) Quake clears the god flag whenever the player spawns on a map (host_cmd.c), so a teleport or door that loads a map turns god mode off without a word (the original keeps it). The session that showed the player killed ("you have been killed by Guard") had set god mode before a teleport that loaded the map, so fact 2 was enough there; fact 1 is read from the code. Planned: the combat layer skips the player's damage in god mode, and god mode survives a map load. |
| [COMBAT-SHIELD-EFFECT-NO-ARMOR-61](bugs/COMBAT-SHIELD-EFFECT-NO-ARMOR-61.md) | A Shield effect on the player does not lower the damage of the blows that land on the player | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker INVENTORY-ARMOR-RATING-61, found there). OpenMW 0.51 mwclass/npc.cpp getArmorRating adds the Shield effect's magnitude to the armour rating, and a blow landing on an actor is reduced by that rating. The player's combat sheet (aw_combat.c AW_CombatPlayerSheet, aw_inventory.c inv_combat) holds the worn pieces and the unarmored rating only, so a Shield changes nothing in a fight; the inventory window's rating (AW_CombatPlayerArmorRating) already adds it. Planned: the same magnitude added where a blow on the player is reduced, read at the blow (the effect can start and end during a fight). |

| [REST-CENSUS-NO-CELL-ID-61](bugs/REST-CENSUS-NO-CELL-ID-61.md) | The rest window offers Rest in the Census and Excise Office, a cell the game marks as no sleeping | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker REST-WAIT-59). The game data marks the Census and Excise Office as a cell where sleeping is not allowed, but in the office the T window opens in Rest mode, and a rest there brings the level-up box; dbg cell there answers that the map has no cell number. Cause: the map does carry its cell keys (_aw_cell_int 763 and its cell ID), but the reader of the map's world entity that dbg cell, the debug HUD and the rest window share stopped at the first value longer than 127 bytes. The compiled rooms (the Census and Excise Office, the Imperial Prison Ship) carry their light grid rows, about 980 bytes each, before the cell keys, so both read as rooms without a cell. CHIM rooms carry no light grid there and were read right. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: a long value is read to its end and kept cut, so the keys after it are found; native test tests/aga_hud_test.c with light grid rows before the keys. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine: dbg cell in the office answers INT 763, "Seyda Neen, Census and Excise Office", and T opens the window with the game line that resting here is illegal and Enter: Wait. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

| [PLACED-PIT-AXE-NO-FOCUS-61](bugs/PLACED-PIT-AXE-NO-FOCUS-61.md) | The iron shardaxe in the Seyda Neen pit is drawn but shows no item box and cannot be taken | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker WORLD-OBJECT-PLACEMENT-59). The items index lists the iron shardaxe, unowned, in Seyda Neen (-2, -10) at -13088 -74893 102, and the game draws it there, but no item box shows and E takes nothing. Cause, measured in game with aw_placed aim (a check command that prints what the aim test makes of each row near the eye): the axe lies in a dip, about 40 map units below the eye, and its origin is under the ground surface: the line of sight from the eye to the origin stops 8.3 to 8.4 map units short of it (the test allows 6), even with the crosshair 0.8 units from it at 27 units. The aim test only looked at the item's origin: how near the view line passes it (4 map units) and whether the origin itself can be seen; a long item lying with its origin at one end, or sunk into the ground, could not be aimed at. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: a row the placed list draws is aimed at where the view ray enters its model's box, turned and scaled as it is drawn, at the distance of that point, and the line of sight is tested to that point, as the original and OpenMW 0.51 test the activation ray against the object itself; rows the map draws itself keep the origin test. Native tests in tests/aga_focus_pickup_test.c. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast), from 47 game units south of the axe: the ray meets the axe's model at 36.8 map units with the view pitched down 80 degrees, the box shows "Iron Shardaxe, Weight: 30, Value: 100" with E: Take, and E takes it (the world change list counts it taken; the axe is gone from the spot). The gold coin nearby, which the ray misses, is still aimed at and taken through the origin test. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

| [INVENTORY-PREVIEW-STALE-61](bugs/INVENTORY-PREVIEW-STALE-61.md) | The inventory character preview does not change when equipment is put on or taken off in the window | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open (shipped, awaiting confirmation) | - | - | - | Fixed in source (709d1399) and shipped in v0.0.61; awaiting confirmation: in the inventory window of a numbered build, each equip and unequip seen changing the character preview at once. Before: Open, v0.0.61 (tracker INVENTORY-EQUIP-CLOTHES-PREVIEW-61). With the window open, Equip and Unequip on a row change the worn set at once, but the preview keeps an earlier picture (seen on v0.0.61-dev1: the bare body with pants, shirt and shoes worn, no cuirass 1 s and 4 s after it went on, the robe kept after it came off; 4 preview renders for 7 changes). The third-person body is right each time. Cause: the parts of a changed outfit load over several frames (at most 40 ms of loading a frame, so that a change never stalls a frame) and the body keeps the previous outfit until they are all in; the window rendered its one picture in the first frame after the change, so of the previous outfit, and kept it. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: the picture waits until the new parts are all loaded (the kept picture shown meanwhile, at most 5 s), then is rendered once, as OpenMW redraws its preview after the new parts are attached; native test tests/aga_inventory_ui_test.c. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): with the window open, the iron cuirass put on, the pants taken off, the common robe put on and the pants put on again each show in the preview 1 s and 4 s after the change, 5 renders for 5 pictures; the third-person body wears the same. The window waited 3 to 8 frames for the parts each time. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |
| [EQUIP-SHARDAXE-REFUSED-61](bugs/EQUIP-SHARDAXE-REFUSED-61.md) | Equipping the iron shardaxe is refused while the iron longsword can be equipped | low | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker PLAYER-GEAR-VISUAL-59). With one iron shardaxe carried, equip is refused ("Diagnostic inventory equip refused."), while the iron longsword is equipped at once. Cause: the inventory catalogue marks a weapon or shield as one the engine can equip only when it has no enchantment at all, and the iron shardaxe carries a Cast When Strikes enchantment. The same rule refused 191 weapons with Cast When Strikes, 59 with Cast When Used and 20 shields with Cast When Used in the v0.0.61-dev1 catalogue. Fix on the v0.0.61 line (the catalogue step, tools/prepare_inventory.py): a weapon or shield whose enchantment does nothing while it is merely held (Cast When Strikes, Cast When Used) is equipped as any other; only a worn item's Constant Effect enchantment is an active effect (OpenMW 0.51), and those stay refused until constant effects are applied. The strike effect itself is not cast yet: WEAPON-STRIKE-ENCHANT-NOT-CAST-61. Test tests/test_inventory_assets.py. Checked in game on a Seyda Neen MiniWind image built from the fix (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): the iron shardaxe is equipped at once, held in the right hand, drawn in first person and in third person, and unequipped again. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

Fixed once a numbered build with it is checked in game. |
| [DIALOGUE-ARROWS-MOVE-POINTER-60](bugs/DIALOGUE-ARROWS-MOVE-POINTER-60.md) | In the dialogue window the Up and Down keys move the mouse pointer instead of the topic selection | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 | open (shipped, awaiting confirmation) | - | - | - | Fixed in source (2842c87e, gate 8000) and shipped in v0.0.62-dev1; awaiting confirmation: Up and Down seen moving the topic selection, not the pointer, in the dialogue window of a numbered build with the shipped emulator settings. The label is inferred: a stack word can be a stale pointer from an earlier call, and the active DOS packet, its owner and any pending device request are not checked. What the check establishes is a guest DOS wait with the completion layer unresolved. Three causes, each measured with the per-frame file counter: the player's assembled body (21 parts loaded in one frame, each opened three times), the compiled scripts' journal names (a 16 KB buffer refilled twice per topic, 6.9 s), and the actor rows (a binary search on disk with a 16 KB buffer, about 1 s). It went unnoticed because a perf-only failure does not stop a build and the failure watcher did not read the perf guard (fixed 2026-11-02, FAILURE_LOOKUP 151). Next: find which change since the baseline made the bake of the Vivec units about 3.5 times the CPU (related: BUILD-RESIDENT-BAKE-SLOWER-52, BUILD-RESIDENT-HAIR-SLOWER-54); fix it, or record the new cost as the baseline with a dated reason. |

| [BUILD-DISK-NEED-UNKNOWN-52](bugs/BUILD-DISK-NEED-UNKNOWN-52.md) | A public build can die halfway when the disk fills: the only space check runs once at the start, against a fixed 20 GiB, not what the release really takes | high | v0.0.50 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51_final_d74cc652) | open | - | - | - | Reported by a tester (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26): their v0.0.50 build from the public repository stopped when the disk ran out; the free-space check runs only before the first stage and asks a fixed 20 GiB (AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB), however much the build needs. The maintainer: a gate check from the start, compared with the release s own build size, automatically against the previous known good build with about 20 % extra. Fix: every passing build records its measured full-build footprint (peak bytes of the workspace, the caches and the scratch, per file system); the release ships the last known good build s figure in the repository; before any stage the preflight asks for that figure plus 20 % on each file system and stops with the numbers when it is short; each stage checks its own last measured bytes plus 20 % before it starts; a gate test fails when the shipped footprint is missing or older than the release. The maintainer (2026-10-26 15:20 +0200 / 2026-10-26 13:20 UTC): the margin about 30 % or more, depending on the dependencies; the need counts everything a fresh build takes, not only the workspace: the builder images (about 2.2 GB each), the Morrowind game data copied into the Docker volume, the caches, the storage pool and the scratch. Measured 2026-10-26: the build runs alone take 19 GB (v0.0.51 final) and 16 GB (v0.0.52-dev3), on top of the shared pool and caches. Fix written (2026-10-26 19:45 +0200 / 2026-10-26 17:45 UTC, v0.0.53 builder, branch v0.0.53-disk): tools/disk_need.py. The check runs first in every image build (tools/build.py right after the options are read: build.sh, build.cmd and the build inside Docker), before the builder image is built (tools/build_docker.py, where Docker storage is visible from the host) and before the game data is copied into a volume (tools/run_docker.py, checked inside the image); and before each stage against that stage's own last figure (tools/build_profile.py start). The need per file system: the last known good build's figure (the larger of the shipped config/disk-footprint.json and this workspace's newest passing build) plus disk_margin_percent (30), less the cache and pool when the workspace already holds a passing build's, the workspace never below min_free_gib (35); both in config/build-defaults.json as machine settings that key no stage (tools/build_cache.py keys that file without them; AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB, AMIWIND_DISK_MARGIN_PERCENT and AMIWIND_DISK_WATCH were keyed environment before: now ignored), also --min-free-gib and --disk-margin-percent. Every passing build writes RUN/disk-footprint.json (run folder bytes, scratch peak from the free space sampled every 5 s, cache and pool growth, game data, per-stage peak growth); tools/disk_need.py ship RUN puts it into the repository. First figure, measured read-only on the build volume: the v0.0.52 final's run folder 15.47 GiB (dev3 the same), storage pool objects written in the v0.0.52 cycle 28.84 GiB (an over-count), game data 1.79 GiB, builder image 2.0 GiB: a fresh native build needs about 58 GiB, Docker about 63 GiB. Gate tests: tests/test_disk_need.py (no stage re-keyed by the settings, a stage stops before it starts, a passing build writes its figure, the shipped figure exists and is not older than the release, the guides state the need). Open until a build writes the first measured figure with stage figures. Gate 4048 (2026-10-26 20:14 +0200 / 2026-10-26 18:14 UTC) stopped on tests/test_run_docker (a missing --input-volume must be refused before any Docker run): the volume check now runs right before the game data copy when there is one, otherwise right after the input checks and before the build container is made. |

| [SKEL-RUNTIME-COST-52](bugs/SKEL-RUNTIME-COST-52.md) | The skeletal prototype poses every vertex twice a drawn frame, with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions each: it must cost what a baked frame costs | high | v0.0.52-dev1 (v0.0.52-dev-source-92f2e8ac) | open | - | - | - | Open (method C, docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the first working version poses an actor s vertices into a scratch frame (bone matrix, quantised with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions, which the 68040 has no hardware instruction for) and the alias path then transforms them again: about twice today s per-vertex work, every drawn frame, estimated at several ms per 1,500-vertex actor on a 25 MHz 68040 (not measured). The method itself costs what baked frames cost: (1) fold each bone s matrix into the one per-vertex transform (view x model x bone, the light direction turned into each bone s space once), so each vertex is transformed once, no divisions or conversions; (2) pose an actor only when its frame changes (alias frames change about 10 times a second, drawn frames 20 to 30); (3) actors on the same table frame share the bone pose; (4) far actors pose less often and skip the joint blend. Acceptance: the frame time of the MiniWind animation stage (SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52) and of CHIM Balmora on the slow-CPU preset no worse than with today s baked actors. Render plan (2026-10-25 22:11 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:11 UTC, after reading AmiQuake s r_alias.c and r_main.c): the actor stays one entity (one box, one light sample, one dynamic light pass, the existing triangle drawing); per bone one combined view x model x bone matrix and the light direction in bone space; the builder sorts vertices by bone so the inner loop keeps one matrix per run (a rigid vertex = a baked vertex s work); pose only on a table-frame change (about 8 a second, a few thousand float operations per actor a second); per-frame ready-made matrices would cost 1.9 to 3.8 MB for the common table and are not worth it; blending between table frames can be switched off (nearest frame). A part that looks wrong rigid and costs too much blended may keep a small shared baked deformation, measured. Progress (2026-10-25 23:46 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:46 UTC): (1) r_alias.c keeps posed frames (8 slots, least recently drawn out; key model, header place, table frame): an actor is posed only when its table frame changes (about 8 a second against 20 to 30 draws) and actors of one model on one frame share the pose; every other draw is a baked frame's work. (2) AW_SkelPoseVerts folds each bone's matrix once with the rest scale and the alias quantisation: per vertex one 3 x 4 transform per bone used, no division; the byte rounding adds 1.5 x 2^23 and reads the mantissa instead of a float-to-integer conversion (the 68040 has no FINTRZ: it traps into the emulation). Native tests within one byte of the builder; compiles for 68040 and 68060 at -O1 and -O2. Not yet measured on the slow-CPU preset (the animation stage). Baked: alias 25.7 ms median (25.6 to 26.0) for 2 alias models drawn, view 1,134 ms, frame 1,261 ms. Skeletal: alias 33.7 ms median (33.5 to 76.0) for 3 alias models drawn, view 1,142 ms, frame 1,271 ms; the 4 lines at about 76 ms are the seconds in which the residents' idle stepped to a new table frame (posing). Per drawn model that is 12.8 ms baked against 11.2 ms skeletal when drawn from the pose cache and about 25 ms when posed. The whole frame was 9 ms (0.7 %) slower at the median and up to 57 ms (4.5 %) slower when posing. Not like for like in one respect: the skeletal build drew one more alias model at this pose (al 3 against 2). Acceptance not met yet: posing costs about twice a baked frame per model. The animated stage (8 actors cycling) on the slow preset is not measured yet. Profiled and cut (2026-10-26 09:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 07:57 UTC). Setup: dbg rcount times the posing (b16bb912: RT_SKELPOSE and RT_SKELVERTS inside the alias time, the kp field with poses made and pose-cache hits), slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 x14), 32 MB, Balmora arrival pose, residents idle, aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Before (b16bb912): one pose was 0.80 ms of bones (AW_SkelPose) and 13.2 ms of vertices (AW_SkelPoseVerts), about 14 ms in all; the vertices are 94 % of it. 871d87e6: a whole frame takes its one key with no blend, square root or division; the never-moving bones are made once per table; the vertex loop has its transforms written out on direct i16 reads. A pose is now 0.61 ms of bones and 9.5 ms of vertices (-28 %). Also fixed there: a forced animation stood still on a slow machine (frames over 0.5 s gave dt 0). 38d6c751: 32 posed frames when AW_TryMalloc allows (the 8 kept slots at 16 MB), so idle residents (an 8-frame loop) stop posing after their first loop. Like for like on one HEAD (3715e8c4), the same pose: baked (--npc-anim-type 1) alias 25.7 ms median, frame 1,272 ms; skeletal alias 33.2 ms, frame 1,275 ms (+0.2 %), with 0 poses in every sampled second. The skeletal side drew 3 alias models against 2 (the extra one passes the cull, likely on the skeletal model's larger box: nothing more is visible in the stills), so per drawn model it is 11.1 ms skeletal against 12.8 ms baked. Worst case, the stage with 8 actors changing group every frame: 8 poses a frame at 0.62 + 8.8 ms each, alias 293 ms against 216 ms held, frame 1.73 s against 1.64 s (+5.6 %). Repair: record each stage's run-folder reads with their SHA-256 and refuse only when one of those differs (whole-output compare kept as the fallback for records without them); the preflight then names the stages that follow a rebuilt stage's outputs as conditional, not as reused Seen again (2026-10-26 00:17 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:17 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try4): an engine change confined to aw_items.h (a parser prototype) and aw_skel.h (the table struct) rebuilt world-flora, chim and chim-town-seyda, whose keys hold every engine header they compile for the struct sizes of their heap checks; the sizes they measure did not change.
