| [BUILD-ORDERED-MAP-SCAN-51](bugs/BUILD-ORDERED-MAP-SCAN-51.md) | The pool map that hands results back in input order scans every held future on each turn: the main process works O(n squared) while large maps run | medium | v0.0.51-dev1 | open | - | - | - | Open (25 October 2026): found profiling the main process of a cached CHIM validation on the v0.0.51-dev1 world (22 workers): ordered_map 8.2 s of its own, Future.done 5.2 million calls (4 s), the _running count 3.8 million (3.5 s). With a cost every item is submitted largest first, so pending holds every result not yet handed back (up to all 1351); each loop turn counts the running ones over all of pending (_running) and builds the wait list over all of pending. Repair: count and wait only on the submitted-and-running set (at most the limit). | [CHIM-ROOM-HEART-CHAMBER-LOAD-50](bugs/CHIM-ROOM-HEART-CHAMBER-LOAD-50.md) | Entering Akulakhan's Chamber when it cannot load stops the game with an error at the console instead of refusing at the door | critical | v0.0.50 (2026_10_24_v0.0.50_final_ffb87463) | open | - | - | - | 10 November 2026 (v0.0.64-dev4 line): a room that cannot load no longer stops the game; it returns the player to the place they came from (Load failed ... Returning to balmora). The chamber itself now loads at 32 MB with room type 2 (AKULAKHAN-CHAMBER-32MB-STALL-53). The heart of the chamber is placed and drawn, as a fixed resident with its idle frames only, so it cannot yet play its Death1 animation when struck (ENDGAME-CHAMBER-COLLAPSE-63). Earlier history: Cause found and fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (24 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing: 32 MB got no automatic cache bank (CHIM-AUTO-BANK-CLIFF-51), so the room's 10.1 MiB of models did not fit. With the repaired engine dbg tp heartchamber at 32 MB loads the room in play (365 placements, 135 models, 5.0 s). Open part: a room that cannot load during play still stops at the console instead of refusing at the door PERSISTING in v0.0.52-dev2 (2026-10-26 11:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 09:18 UTC, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB, image 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev2_dev2_3715e8c4). Seyda Neen, then Balmora (dbg cam recall bm3), then dbg tp heartchamber ended in Host_Error: CHIM room map maps/rifa4ef181ed.chim: its room record or models cannot be loaded. The room found 2 MiB of the free Fast RAM for its models (and 1994 KiB of the Hunk) and a model of the store could not be loaded. Afterwards: Memory now 4795 KiB free, largest block 4492 KiB. Loaded as the first map it works: 4 MiB taken, Memory now 1291 KiB free, largest block 1177 KiB, zone 1476 KiB free. The difference was the skeletal session memory held since the town: the animation tables and the large pose cache, 1589 KiB. Fixed in 2d49fb88 (gate 4032): before Chim_RoomGrow measures the free Fast RAM, the engine flushes its skeletal models from the model cache and gives back the tables and the large pose cache, all made again on demand (aw_skel_release.c). Checked on a play copy of the dev2 image with the 2d49fb88 engine swapped in: the same route loads the chamber (1589 KiB given back first, 3 MiB of Fast RAM and 1994 KiB of the Hunk taken, room 148 models 18129 KiB loaded in 2701 ms). Afterwards Memory now is 2200 KiB free, largest block 2058 KiB; the zone has 420 KiB free, largest run 417 KiB. The Heart's structure and a figure before it are in view. Still open at 32 MB: 2 model loads fail both after the town and as the first map (zone failed requests, the last 250624 bytes after the town, 60112 as the first map); at 64 MB 0 fail. Which models these are (Dagoth Ur's full model and the Heart's actor are the suspects, outside the build gate's count) is not identified yet. Stills: clips/v0.0.52 akulakhan_chamber_32mb_after_balmora, 32mb_first_map, 64mb_after_balmora. 2026-10-26 12:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 10:53 UTC: named and fixed (v0.0.52, gate 4034). The two failed loads at 32 MB were not models left out: zone failed: model 1639 (x/ex_dwrv_enter00, a Dwemer entrance of the room, 250,580 bytes) and model 4991 (i/in_akulacave00 tile 5,8, 147,092 bytes) are the requests that made the room grow (try 1 full, the free Fast RAM bank; try 2 full, the Hunk rest; try 3 loaded): every model was in place (room: 148 models, 18,129 KiB; zone used = the gate's need), neither Dagoth Ur (an actor model in Quake's cache, not the zone) nor the Heart. The console now says so (room: loaded whole on try 3; it grew 2 times, each after a request the full zone refused). The real shortfall was the margin: after Balmora the room bank was 3 MiB (zone 420 KiB free) because the tables given back do not join the largest block and the bank was cut to whole MiB. Fixed: the room bank in 64 KiB steps (CHIM_ROOM_GRAIN); a registry of re-makeable session memory (aw_fastrelease.c AW_FastReleaseRegister/AW_FastReleaseAll, 8 releasers, one console line each with free and largest block before and after) called before the CHIM cache banks at start-up, -chimcache and a room's growth (never per frame), the skeletal tables and posed frames its first releaser; a console line of the free Fast RAM at the room step. Measured at 32 MB after Balmora (FS-UAE, dev2 image, new engine): given back 1,589 KiB, free 4,696 -> 6,286 KiB, largest 4,488 -> 5,512 KiB, bank 3,456 KiB (was 3,072), zone 804 KiB free (was 420), Memory now 1,814 KiB free, largest 1,671. The room heap gate counts the worse route now (engine_limits MEASURED_ROOM 5,512 KiB: bank 3,456 KiB; the chamber needs 19,093,616 of 19,968,800, its walk leaves 848 KiB, measured 804) and the actors: the animation tables their skeletal models name and the pose cache must fit what the room bank leaves (CHIM_ROOM_KEEP 2 MiB), else the gate fails (the chamber: humanoid table 579,816 + pose cache 393,984 = 990,188 bytes). Tests: tests/test_fast_release.py (native registry with stubs, call sites, every MEMF_LARGEST sizing listed), aga_chim_world_test roomgrow, test_chim_room_heap; m68k 4 variants clean. 2026-10-26 13:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 11:02 UTC: committed 9741c99c (gate 4034 passed, 5,913 tests); in-game check in the dev3 image. |

The payload preflight planned 2.45 GB of boot payload on 2 partitions; the CHIM room actor bake then wrote its fitted actor models inside the step and the payload reached 3.01 GB, 3 partitions (dev2 grew 2.40 -> 2.71 GB and stayed on 2). rc1 actor models are about 6-8 % bigger each than dev2 (room batches: 6,844 models, 2,727 MB against 6,938, 2,593 MB) and about 2,000 more distinct models reach the image. Worked around: a payload that only grew is laid out from the staged files (layout_plan.follows_or_grew); require_minimal and the headroom gate still decide. The real fix (v0.0.49, the maintainer asked that the size be figured out from what has been created): the room actor bake becomes its own cached stage before the image, so the plan is computed from files that exist. |

| [BUILD-PLAYER-VIEW-UNDERUSED-48](bugs/BUILD-PLAYER-VIEW-UNDERUSED-48.md) | The image step player view remade all 80 player bodies in every build on four fresh worker pools (2m05s at 16.2 of 24 cores) | high | v0.0.48-dev2 (2026_10_22_v0.0.48-dev2_miniwind-balmora-rooms-bsp_1336ba94) | open (shipped, awaiting confirmation) | - | - | deferred | Fixed in source (dc440813) and shipped in v0.0.66-dev2; awaiting confirmation by a build that bakes the player bodies (the dev11 build took them from the unit cache in 12 s): its player view stage time and cores against the 95 minutes of the v0.0.62 release build. Before: REGRESSED in v0.0.62 (fixed in v0.0.48-dev2 before): the image step's player view of the v0.0.62 release build ran 24 cores for about 15 min, 11-12 from about 37 min, 7 after 63 min and 1 core for its last 25 min (95 min in all): each body ran every fitting try one after the other on one core, and the torch bodies waited in a second map for the slowest body. Fix on branch v0.0.63-speed (tools/player_view_schedule.py): one flow, each torch body starts when its body is done; the fitting tries of a body are units of their own, an idle worker starts the next try of a running body, tries no longer needed are stopped; the try that fitted is kept in the unit cache. Same results byte for byte, unit keys unchanged (bake-reach digest 1eeb4b9a...). On the release build's unit times, 24 workers: 95 min before, about 70 min in the first build with the flow, 59 min once the tries are timed, 44 min with the fitted tries known (tests/test_player_view_schedule.py). To confirm on the next build that bakes the bodies. |

| [CHIM-BC-TREE-PYRAMID-BOX-47](bugs/CHIM-BC-TREE-PYRAMID-BOX-47.md) | Bitter Coast trees (flora_bc_tree family) look like a pyramid trunk with a flat box floating above it | medium | v0.0.47-dev1 (2026_10_21_v0.0.47-dev1_dev1-try2_4a2d42b9) | open | - | - | - | 2026-11-10, branch v0.0.64-fence2: the renderer now has a see-through face kind. The converter marks every texture whose alpha channel leaves at least 1 % of its texels under half alpha (name prefix "{", palette index 255 for its transparent texels; other textures keep their bytes and unit keys), and the engine draws those faces in a separate pass after the walls, z-tested, skipping index 255 (aw_fence, dbg fence; off by default until a measured A/B on the next full build decides). Proof pending: the cobweb in Andrano Ancestral Tomb and a hanging growth outdoors with the switch off and on. Bitter Coast crowns that use see-through textures are covered by the same pass; their geometry is unchanged here. Earlier: Open: cause unknown; proposed fix direction: crossed vertical planes with the tree's outline (alpha kept), angle impostors as the alternative; A/B first, nothing built. Seen again in v0.0.62-dev1 (PERSISTING): Bitter Coast trees with fungi growing on them are drawn as a distorted stand-in, a dome-like shape at flora_bc_tree_08, taken from its collision-only model, so the bracket fungus (Hypha Facia) beside it floats in the air (FUNGI-FLOATING-62; the earlier floating-tree fix BC-TREE-FLOATING-60 covered trees that did not reach the ground, a different fault). Decided direction: (1) a tree whose parts can be picked or touched gets a very low-polygon solid trunk with measured dimensions, no part thinner than half its original width and no new gaps (the method in the mesh reduction notes, MESH-REDUCTION-SEAMS-62); (2) purely decorative foliage can be transparent planes or sprites; (3) fungi are seated on the trunk surface. |

| [CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43](bugs/CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43.md) | Travelling from Seyda Neen to Balmora sometimes hangs on the Loading screen (boot smoke, 2 of about 5 runs) | high | v0.0.43-dev1 (2026_10_17_v0.0.43-dev1_full-batch2_7ac15b1) | open | - | - | - | Open, in the test sessions only (they serve the remote console from a host folder mounted as a drive; a player's game has no such drive). The cause read from the emulator's source on 16 November 2026 and shown in a test session the same day. The three stops examined with the packet read off the game's stack on the v0.0.66-dev10 image were all requests to the test sessions' remote-console folder, a host folder FS-UAE serves as a drive from a host thread: an open answered not found, a write of 320 bytes completed, an open for output completed; each finished on the host side with its results in the packet, every handler idle, the game asleep on its reply. In FS-UAE 3.1.66 that host thread announces a completion by setting one bit of a shared interrupt-request word with a plain read-modify-write, and the emulator thread clears another device's bit of the same word the same way on every interrupt-request change (a2065.cpp rethink_a2065, before its configured check); an overlap loses the announcement, no dummy message reaches the handler, and the finished request stays on the handler's private queue. Upstream made these operations atomic in December 2016; the 3.1.66 line does not have it. Players have no such drive. Way out for the sessions: deterministic = 1 (no host thread for host folders), asked for by tests/sessions/load_repeat_hops_det.txt; the stall examination now prints the handler's state word of the stuck request (-1 = finished by the host side, the handler never told). Shown in a plain repeat session on the same image: it stopped after nine arena pit loads with the game's packet a FINDINPUT of AWCTL:cmd.txt (the remote console's poll of its missing command file, its result already set) and the handler's state word for it -1: the emulator's host side finished the request and the handler was never told. The way out, deterministic = 1, is being measured by the same comparison. |

Same files and the same reports (tests/test_chim_pack_layout.py, tests/test_chim_check_pool.py). Both steps now print their parts with time and cores in the build log; the next full build shows whether the gaps are gone. Before: 3 November 2026 (v0.0.59-dev3, 1,351 frames): CHIM world pack 2 min 14 s on one core, CHIM validation 1 min 48 s on 6.0 of 23 cores. Report (2026-10-31, the v0.0.57 release build 2026_10_31_v0.0.57_full-v0.0.57-release_7ff625e, with dca2eb3d and af01f913): the tail from the validation's start to the zone walk's end 160 s (dev5: 273 s): validation 92.6 s at 6.6 cores (dev5 148.9 s at 7.5; its unit-cache key now worked out beside the world build), heap gate 4.1 s, the stats 34.5 s at 18.9 cores beside the zone walk 60.9 s at 20.6 (dev5: stats 23.5 s at 2.0, then the zone walk 88.8 s). Still serial: the pack, 110.4 s on 1.0 core (dev5 136.4 s; serial by design, ids in walk order). Left for v0.0.58: the validation's main process (pickling, the ordered_map poll loop, load_world, measure; see below). Stays open. PERSISTING in v0.0.57-dev5 (full build 095612e9, 2026-10-30): after the world build the tail ran pack 136 s on 1.0 core (serial by design: ids are handed out in walk order), validation 149 s on 7.5 of 24 cores, stats 23.5 s on 2 cores, zone walk 89 s on 15. Fixed in part for v0.0.57 (2026-10-31): the stats run in a thread beside the zone walk, after the heap gate (about 23 s off the tail); and the validation's unit-cache key (pass_cache digests of chim/validate.py, 13.6 s measured cold, about 20 s in the build's profile) is worked out in a thread beside the world build (measured: 13.6 s -> 0.0 s at the validation). Profile of the validation on the dev5 world (cProfile, 23 jobs, 152 s, the same as the build's 149 s): the main process is the limit, not the workers: pickling tasks and results (dump 8.5 s, loads 7.6 s, writes 8.2 s), the shared ordered_map loop (10.6 s own time, 5.4 million future.done() calls), load_world 35 s, measure 25 s, visibility_report 16 s, ownership 16 s, ring_needs 5 s. What is left needs the per-frame cross-checks to return smaller results and ordered_map to wait on completed futures instead of polling all of them (build_parallel.py is in nearly every stage key: a v0.0.58 item). Before: Fixed in part on v0.0.51-dev (25 October 2026): CHIM validation's main process packed the chunk trees as one array per node and decoded every visibility row bit by bit; with a warm unit cache on the v0.0.51-dev1 world it took 116 s, now 94 s, 0 failures; the v0.0.51-dev2 perf guard passed (validation 17.5 of 23 cores, cold cache). Left: the in-order map's own scanning (BUILD-ORDERED-MAP-SCAN-51), a few serial seconds of set-up, and the CHIM world pack on one core (ids handed out in walk order). Details on the page PERSISTING (2026-10-25 21:48 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:48 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try2 d27706d6): CHIM world pack 2m11s at 1.0 of 23.3 cores; CHIM validation 2m02s at 5.5; the chim stage idle at 2.12 of 24 cores for 2m50s; chim-rooms-vivec_city 57.7s at 2.26 of 22.2. Also (2026-10-25 23:31 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:31 UTC, same build): CHIM validation on 5.6 of 24 cores for 65 s with 1,278 units queued and 23 running (the stage's pools run fewer units than allowed). PERSISTING (2026-10-26 01:07 +0200 / 2026-10-25 23:07 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try4 d62a2ad3, perf guard FIX-NOW): CHIM validation 3.94 of 24 cores for 3m22s; also CHIM world pack 1.00 of 24 for 2m38s and the image's layout and partitions 1.5 of 24 for about 3 minutes. Seen again in v0.0.65: a guard fights with a weapon nobody sees. Cause found: the people of the NPC library (the standing models of the people outside the town residents, most guards among them) had no carried-item tag at all: in the v0.0.65 release build none of its 423 models had one, while the 1,357 resident models carry theirs. The guard's record does give him a weapon (the actor table equips a steel spear from his levelled list). Fixed on v0.0.66-actorrecords: the library writes the same tag the residents get for every skeletal model whose person carries a weapon or shield (288 of the 423 models; about 100 bytes a tag, the item models shared), beside the bake so no model is baked again; AMIWIND_NPC_LIBRARY_ITEMS=0 turns it off. Not yet checked in game (no build ran). |

| [NPC-BAKED-WHOLE-DUPLICATION-33](bugs/NPC-BAKED-WHOLE-DUPLICATION-33.md) | Every NPC appearance is baked whole: shared body parts are converted again for each actor, and equipment cannot change | high | v0.0.32 | open | - | - | - | PERSISTING in v0.0.48-rc1 (24 October 2026): stage 1 of docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md (parts library, gallery from parts) is built; stage 2 (residents from the library) and stage 3 (the engine composed-model loader) were never built, and v0.0.48 baked the 1,769 interior residents whole, every one with its own 64 animation frames: the rc1 image carries about 1,500 MB of actor models against 297 MB for Morrowind.bsa (ROOM-RESIDENT-MODELS-SIZE-48). Stages 2 and 3 come first in v0.0.49 (docs/ROADMAP.md, "The actors get the CHIM rule"). The maintainer (2026-10-25 17:28 +0200 / 2026-10-25 15:28 UTC): the whole idea is that all actors use the shared lookup table for actions; the common actions need shared lookup tables. The animations are baked per actor too: every mover holds its own walk, run and attack frames (992 MB of the 1.5 GB of actors in v0.0.51), so the region actors got no movers at all (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35). Wanted: one shared animation table per skeleton, the body parts as a library, each actor composed and skinned once at load (docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md stages 2-3); first measure the load-time skinning cost of one town on the 68030/68040 target. Raised to the v0.0.52 list after the door table (DOOR-ENTRANCE-AUDIT-51). Progress (2026-10-25 21:20 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:20 UTC, v0.0.52 Skeletons Of Society, method C in docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the shared humanoid table holds every group (139 of 139, the combat phases and the inventory poses included; walking, running, sneaking, swimming and jumping held in place); the engine reads the table and a model s skeletal block and poses it per drawn frame (aw_skel.c, r_alias.c), the protocol carries frames past 255 (U_AW_EXT AWU_FRAME2); the first real skeletal actor, a Balmora resident, is 359,184 bytes for every motion against 395,700 for today s idle-only bake (plus a mover of about 501 KB), engine pose within 0.20 model units of the baked frames at idle (the two-bone joint blend up to 1.24 units in run and death poses); box 66 x 81 x 41 units, 0 of 5,046 frames clamped. Open: SKEL-VERTEX-LIMIT-52, SKEL-TABLE-SIZE-52, the game logic for every group (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35), the in-game prototype and SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52. Payload plan (2026-10-25 21:34 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:34 UTC; the maintainer: the disk space is too large, it should not be in the package): skeletons alone remove the 992 MB of baked frames and the second (mover) model, but each character s mesh and skin stay stored once per character (about two thirds skin): about 1,770 characters x about 360 KB, roughly 600 MB. The parts library (each body part once, measured at about 67 MB for every resident against about 535 MB baked whole) assembled at load is the other half: v0.0.52 takes both, with a hard actor budget in the size ledger. Ship rule (2026-10-25 21:41 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:41 UTC, the maintainer: would that include the 990 MB of prebaked frames in the game? No): from v0.0.52 a shipped build carries no baked actor frames and no mover models; the baked method is a test-build option only (the animation stage A/B, a few MB); a kit check refuses a shipped build that has them. Default (2026-10-25 21:41 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:41 UTC, the maintainer: skeletons by default, they take a fraction; whoever wants the prebaked frames compiles the game with them): --npc-anim-type 2 is the builder default; 1 only when chosen at build time. Design (2026-10-25 21:58 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:58 UTC, the maintainer: can the reused modules carry the movement; baking is impossible once actors change clothes): parts carry no motion; 479 of 519 rigid parts drawn with their one bone s matrix (Quake-style, the cost of a static model), about 40 skin parts take the joint blend; the motion is the one shared table. Movement sets per part would be per-part baking, the same mistake; a baked actor cannot change clothes without a bake per outfit. docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md Getting NPC movement right. Measured again (2026-10-25 23:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:54 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try3): the boot payload is 3,028,309,475 bytes, id1/progs 1,996,183,591 of it (the baked actors and their mover models): 820 units had to move off DH0 onto the world volumes. Builder (2026-10-26 00:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:54 UTC, v0.0.52, method C step C3): --npc-anim-type 1 or 2 in tools/build.py, default 2 (skeletal); 1 = the baked kit exactly as before. Type 2: every humanoid resident (prepare_area.build_resident: towns, Seyda Neen, rooms) and actor-library model (npc_library) is one rest frame on the shared table of its skeleton (progs/humanoid.awsk; progs/humanoid_f.awsk, the female groups layered over the common ones as OpenMW stacks xbase_anim_female over xbase_anim; progs/humanoid_kna.awsk, the beasts), each written once; the kit layout names the table's frames; no mover models, no baked frames; the type is in the resident stages' keys (AMIWIND_NPC_ANIM_TYPE) and the actor library's appearance keys. Size ledger (the base game's 2,612 placed NPC records, the react+full profile, files before resident sharing): type 1 3,222 MB for the 2,515 it bakes (models 1,256 MB, movers 1,957 MB), type 2 512 MB for the same 2,515 plus 1.8 MB of tables (about 1,281 KB against 204 KB an actor); docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md. Open: the in-game check, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52, the kit check that refuses baked frames in a shipped build, the parts library (the skins and meshes per character are what is left). Kit check (2026-10-26 01:44 +0200 / 2026-10-25 23:44 UTC): the release guard (the kit tooling) refuses a v0.0.52-or-later release whose image build does not record npc_anim_type 2 (build-state.json, written by tools/build.py since 471cadcd): no baked actor frames in a shipped build. To confirm on the dev1-try5 build state once written. Progress (v0.0.63, 9 November 2026, IMAGE-BIGGER-THAN-ORIGINAL-62): the whole-baked actor models now share their texture coordinates and triangles (about 78 MB less, in v0.0.63-dev1); their skins can be stored as shared 16x16 tiles (builder option --skin-tiles, experimental, off by default: about 319 MB less on the v0.0.63-dev1 payload, its load time on the Pi 4B to be measured first). |

| [BUILD-EXPANSIONS-31](bugs/BUILD-EXPANSIONS-31.md) | Tribunal and Bloodmoon cannot be converted with today's tools | medium | v0.0.32-dev | open | - | - | - | Open. Found by the whole-world measurement (every object placed, estimated per map, checked on 30 converted maps). v0.0.64 line: the build options --dlc (tribunal, bloodmoon, both or none) and --no-dlc choose the expansion layers (default: every expansion found) and the base world keys no longer depend on which expansion files are present (BUILD-GAME-INPUT-KEY-BROAD-64); the exterior cell list and the interior reader take a master list (Morrowind.esm plus the chosen layers' masters). Not yet wired into the stages: no expansion cell is built. 10 November 2026 (v0.0.64): the expansions have their own save-ID ranges. Tribunal and Bloodmoon rooms take IDs from their own bases of 4096 after the base batch rooms (engine aw_maps.h, generated table aw_layer_table.h from config/room-batches-tribunal.json and config/room-batches-bloodmoon.json, both empty for now); the engine always carries all three lists, so one engine serves every combination, and an ID in an expansion range the table does not name is titled "needs Tribunal" or "needs Bloodmoon". The disk layout planner moves the expansion stores (chimsol, chimiti, chimibm) as whole units like the interior store. No world or content stage of the base build changes: the reuse preflight against the v0.0.63 release build rebuilds the same stages as before the change (only the engine and the image name the new files). Still open: converting the expansions. Open. Found by the whole-world measurement (every object placed, estimated per map, checked on 30 converted maps). |

| [AUDIO-LOAD-29](bugs/AUDIO-LOAD-29.md) | OST crackles under heavy loading | high | v0.0.29-rc1 | open | - | - | - | Fixed in source on v0.0.52-dev (25 October 2026), not built yet: the first load after the intro movie ran the music dry 1-3 times (v0.0.51-dev3 and the final: 0 late, every other load 0 dry). Cause: the music stream reads its next 16 KiB block only from the frame loop (CDAudio_Update) or as the painter's emergency fill; a load holds the frame loop, and the track restarted after the movie with an empty buffer. Now every load-time mixer update (snd_dma.c S_Update_) also pumps the stream's reads (aw_music.c AW_MusicLoadPump, never waits; not under the movie); tests: music_player_test loadpump, aga_loading_audio_test. To verify: the audio smoke of the next dev build, the first load 0 dry, and the maintainer's WinUAE listen. Before: Corrected 25 October 2026 (v0.0.51-dev, not built yet): the first load's 219-319 ms 'gap' and its dry count in the dev1 and dev2 measurements were the intro movie, which plays inside the New Game load, pauses the music and plays its own sound; the load meter timed the paused music. The meter now leaves the movie out and says so, and names the load step at both ends of the longest gap (a trace of the ticks when it passes 150 ms). Measured again (FS-UAE, 32 MB, the dev2 image with the gate 3891 engine, the same five loads): longest gaps 58 (first load, outside a 4,893 ms movie), 43, 52, 115 (Akulakhan's Chamber, world model to entities) and 49 ms, 0 late. The first load still counts the music running dry 3 times outside the movie (likely the music restarting after it; not checked). Before: Fixed in part in source on v0.0.51-dev (24 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing; WinUAE listen pending. Ordinary file and model reads already read in 4 KiB slices with the music serviced between them; the CHIM pack reads (rooms, frames, models: one read of up to megabytes) did not, and now do. Every load prints 'Loading audio: N mixer updates, longest gap X ms (mixes Y ms ahead), K late, music ran dry D times'. FS-UAE, 32 MB, same five loads before/after: longest gap Seyda Neen 216/221, prison ship 39/37, census office 55/52, Akulakhan's Chamber 218/204, Balmora 205/46 ms; the mixer mixes 1,486 ms ahead; 0 late in every load. The remaining ~200 ms gaps in Seyda Neen and the chamber are another step of those loads. The opening's crackle (hull to deck, census office) is judged by the maintainer on WinUAE with the v0.0.51 playtest, where the console prints the same lines |

| [INLAND-SHORE-29](bugs/INLAND-SHORE-29.md) | v0.0.29-dev1: Angular/jagged inland shoreline | medium | v0.0.29-dev1 | open | - | - | deferred | Open, needs a world rebuild; plan written, no world code changed. Seen on the v0.0.61 release image: the water edge at shores and ponds runs in saw-tooth steps (Suran, cell 6,-7, and ponds and the outer coast across the map). First suspect: the reduction of the land mesh at the water edge. Plan: (1) measure first, in a container, on the stored terrain of the v0.0.62 release run: per frame, the shoreline vertices (land triangles that cross the water height) whose height or angle jump between neighbours passes a threshold, against the original LAND heights; (2) one world-wide terrain pass in the builder that moves those vertices onto the original surface at the water line, adding no triangles, with a per-area count of moved vertices and a check that the shoreline stays within a set distance of the original; never a local patch. Rebuild cost: the change re-keys the terrain of every CHIM frame, so the chim stage runs again (about 17 to 18 minutes on 24 jobs in the full v0.0.62 build fe90f8e of 8 November 2026) and the image after it; the interiors stage is not touched. To be scheduled for a dev build that re-keys the chim stage anyway (tracker COASTLINE-JAGGED-62). |

Every dated event of every bug, newest first, from the entries' own data (reports, history lines, closure steps, returns, fixes, deferrals; the first notice is the Found in column above). ### Bugs by family

Every bug from v0.0.30 on belongs to one family (bugs with a shared cause or area); the families and their shared rules are in [bug tracking](bugs/README.md#families).

#### Vivec preview frame and its joins to the world (`vivec-frame-edge`)
